name: Washington
about: Every Washington special-design plate. Points come from real registration counts: WA DOL's Special License Plate Annual Report to the Legislature (2023 data) and the 2025 figures reported by the Seattle Times. Brand-new plates are estimates.

sources.title: WA DOL Special License Plate Annual Report (2024)

plates.name: US Air Force
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: The Air Force plate is one of Washington's six Armed Forces plates. Each purchase or renewal sends $28 to the Veterans Stewardship Account, which helps fund the state veterans cemetery and programs for homeless veterans.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: US Army
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: The most popular of Washington's six Armed Forces plates with about 7,700 registered vehicles — ranking 7th overall among all specialty plates statewide. Eligibility requires being a veteran, active duty, reservist, National Guard member, or family of one.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: US Coast Guard
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: Counting every inlet, bay and island, Washington has more than 3,000 miles of tidal shoreline, so there is plenty of water for the Coast Guard to watch over. Like all six Armed Forces plates, it sends $28 per plate to veterans programs.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: US Marine Corps
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: The Marine Corps plate is one of Washington's six Armed Forces plates, open to Marines, veterans, reservists and their families. Each purchase or renewal sends $28 to the Veterans Stewardship Account.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: WA National Guard
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: The Washington National Guard helped with search and rescue after Mount St. Helens erupted in 1980, when the blast flattened about 230 square miles of forest. Guard members still answer the call when floods and wildfires hit the state.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: US Navy
plates.supports: Veterans Stewardship Account ($28/plate; state veterans cemetery, homeless-veteran programs)
plates.fact: With Naval Station Everett and Naval Base Kitsap, Washington is one of the Navy's key home ports. Puget Sound's deep, sheltered water drew the Navy here in the 1890s, when the Bremerton shipyard was founded.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Disabled American Veteran
plates.fact: Unlike most specialty plates, the Disabled American Veteran plate comes with a significant benefit: it waives certain vehicle licensing fees for qualified disabled veterans. Washington has over 500,000 veterans — about 6.5% of the state's adult population.

plates.name: Former Prisoner of War
plates.fact: One of the most restricted plates in Washington — eligibility requires documented status as a former prisoner of war. As the WWII and Korean War generation ages, this plate becomes increasingly rare. A genuine piece of living history on the road.

plates.name: Gold Star Family
plates.fact: The Gold Star designation dates to WWI, when families displayed a gold star in their window for each member serving. A blue star meant serving; gold meant fallen. This plate is available to family members of service members who died in the line of duty.

plates.name: Medal of Honor
plates.supports: Recognition of Medal of Honor recipients
plates.fact: The Medal of Honor is the nation's highest military honor. As of 2025, there are fewer than 70 living Medal of Honor recipients in the entire United States. Washington has produced several recipients, including those from the Pacific Theater of WWII.

plates.name: Military Affiliate Radio
plates.fact: MARS — the Military Affiliate Radio System — is a DoD program using amateur radio operators to provide communication support for the military. One of the original 1993 specialty plates, approved the same year as the Square Dancer. Ham radio meets military service.

plates.name: Purple Heart
plates.fact: The Purple Heart honors service members wounded or killed in combat. It traces back to George Washington's Badge of Military Merit of 1782, which makes it the oldest U.S. military award still given.

plates.name: 988 Veteran Suicide Prevention (emblem)
plates.supports: WDVA veteran & military suicide prevention programs
plates.fact: This is a slim emblem that fits on any Washington plate and shows the 988 crisis line with the words 'There is hope!' Proceeds fund suicide prevention for veterans and service members. Veterans make up about 7% of Washington's population but about 18% of its suicides.

plates.name: Endangered Wildlife – Orca
plates.supports: WA Dept. of Fish & Wildlife orca recovery
plates.fact: Washington's Southern Resident orcas are endangered. The July 2026 census counted 76 whales in J, K and L pods, up two from the year before. They live on salmon and have their own calls, distinct from other killer whales.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Honeybees & Pollinators
plates.supports: WA State Beekeepers Association research & education
plates.fact: This plate shows a monarch, a honey bee and a mason bee among flowers. $28 from each plate goes to the Washington State Beekeepers Association for pollinator research and education, and the plate arrived in 2026.

plates.name: Lighthouses
plates.fact: New Dungeness Lighthouse on the Olympic Peninsula has guided ships since 1857. Volunteers still take turns as keepers, living at the light station for a week at a time.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: San Juan Islands
plates.fact: The San Juan Islands have 172 named islands. They were the scene of the 1859 'Pig War' between the US and Britain, where the only casualty was a pig. An 1872 arbitration put the border west of the islands, so all of them belong to Washington.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: State Flower
plates.fact: Washington's state flower is the coast rhododendron. Women voters picked it in 1892, three years after statehood, and the Legislature made it official in 1949. Plate fees support Meerkerk Rhododendron Gardens on Whidbey Island.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Washington Apple Commission
plates.fact: Washington grows well over half of America's apples, and Wenatchee calls itself the Apple Capital of the World. The state's first apple trees are said to have been planted at the Hudson's Bay Company's Fort Vancouver in 1826.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Washington National Parks
plates.fact: Washington has three national parks: Olympic, Mount Rainier and North Cascades. At 14,410 feet, Mount Rainier carries more glacier ice than any other peak in the lower 48, with more than two dozen glaciers. $28 from each plate goes to Washington's National Park Fund.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures (12,749 per KPQ)

plates.name: Washington State Parks
plates.supports: WA State Parks and Recreation Commission
plates.fact: Deception Pass is Washington's busiest state park, with more than 3 million visitors a year. In 2021 it drew more people than Yosemite National Park. $28 from each plate goes to Washington State Parks.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wildlife – Bear
plates.fact: Washington is home to an estimated 25,000 to 30,000 black bears. Despite the name, many are brown, cinnamon or even blond. $28 from each wildlife plate helps WDFW manage the state's game animals.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2023 report: FY2022 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wildlife – Deer
plates.fact: Washington has black-tailed deer west of the Cascades, mule deer to the east and white-tailed deer in the northeast. The rare Columbia white-tailed deer is recovering at a refuge near Cathlamet.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wildlife – Elk
plates.fact: The Olympic Peninsula is home to Roosevelt elk, the largest elk in North America. Protecting these herds was one reason Olympic National Park was created in 1938.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wildlife – Steelhead
plates.fact: A steelhead is a rainbow trout that heads out to sea and comes back to its home river to spawn. It's the same species with a very different life story. Several Washington runs, including the Snake River's, are protected as threatened.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wild on Washington – Eagle
plates.fact: Washington has one of the highest concentrations of bald eagles in the contiguous US. The Skagit River delta in winter hosts hundreds of eagles feeding on spawned-out salmon — one of the great wildlife spectacles in the Pacific Northwest. The bald eagle was removed from the endangered species list in 2007.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Keep WA Evergreen
plates.fact: Keep WA Evergreen brings back the green-on-white look of Washington's 1970s plates, with an EV logo. Fees help build electric-vehicle charging stations, and you don't need an EV to get one.

plates.name: Smokey Bear
plates.supports: WA Dept. of Natural Resources wildfire prevention
plates.fact: Smokey Bear has been the face of wildfire prevention since 1944. The real Smokey was a cub rescued from a 1950 New Mexico fire who lived out his life at the National Zoo. Washington joins Oregon and Texas in offering a Smokey plate, which funds DNR wildfire prevention.

plates.name: Mount St. Helens
plates.fact: Mount St. Helens erupted on May 18, 1980, lowering its summit by 1,314 feet and flattening about 230 square miles of forest. Each plate sends $28 to the Mount St. Helens Institute for youth education, trail work and science.

plates.name: Seattle Seahawks
plates.supports: Seattle Seahawks Charitable Foundation ($21) & WA State Leadership Board ($7)
plates.fact: The Seahawks plate is Washington's 5th most popular, with about 11,100 vehicles in 2025. For the team's 50th season it got a new design in the classic blue and green, replacing the look used from 2014 to 2025.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Seattle Mariners
plates.supports: WA State Leadership Board youth programs (World Fellows, Sports Mentorship)
plates.fact: Mariners plates sold since 2019 help fund youth programs through the Washington State Leadership Board, including first-generation college scholarships and inclusive sports grants. About 1,100 fans had one in 2025.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Seattle Kraken
plates.fact: The Kraken, named for a legendary sea monster from Scandinavian folklore, became the NHL's 32nd team and played their first game in 2021. Their plate went on sale in May 2021, with most of its proceeds going to the team's One Roof Foundation.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Seattle Sounders FC
plates.supports: Mentor Washington & WA State Leadership Board
plates.fact: Sounders crowds are among the biggest in MLS, averaging about 31,000 a game in 2025, second in the league. The club won MLS Cup in 2016 and 2019, and its plate supports youth mentoring.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Seattle Storm
plates.supports: WA State Leadership Board grants for women's & girls' sports
plates.fact: The Storm have won four WNBA titles (2004, 2010, 2018 and 2020), and Sue Bird spent her whole career in Seattle, from 2002 to 2022. The plate funds grants that open up sports for women and girls.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Ski and Ride
plates.fact: Crystal Mountain near Mount Rainier is Washington's largest ski area. Mount Baker Ski Area holds the record for snowfall in a single season: 1,140 inches (95 feet) in 1998–99.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: State Sport: Pickleball
plates.supports: Seattle Metro Pickleball Association court construction
plates.fact: Pickleball was invented on Bainbridge Island in 1965 by Joel Pritchard, Bill Bell and Barney McCallum, using ping-pong paddles and a plastic ball on a badminton court. It became the state sport in 2022, and this was the nation's first pickleball plate when it went on sale in November 2025.

plates.name: Tennis
plates.supports: City public indoor tennis facility (4+ courts)
plates.fact: The Tennis plate is one of the rarest in Washington, with only about 80 on the road in 2023. Proceeds are set aside to help a city build and maintain a public tennis center with at least four indoor courts.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Wrestling
plates.supports: WA State Wrestling Foundation (college wrestling programs)
plates.fact: About 270 Washington drivers carry the Wrestling plate. Proceeds go to the Washington State Wrestling Foundation to help start and support college wrestling programs.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Washington State University
plates.fact: WSU is Washington's most popular specialty plate, with about 24,100 vehicles in 2025, more than twice as many as the UW plate. Founded in 1890 as the state's land-grant university, WSU sits in the rolling wheat country of the Palouse.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: University of Washington
plates.fact: The UW plate ranks 6th among Washington specialty plates, with about 10,300 vehicles. Founded in 1861, nearly 30 years before statehood, the UW is one of the oldest public universities on the West Coast.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Central Washington University
plates.fact: Central Washington University in Ellensburg was founded in 1891 and is known for its aviation program. For three decades it was home to Washoe, the famous chimpanzee who learned American Sign Language.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Eastern Washington University
plates.fact: Eastern Washington University in Cheney won the FCS national football championship in 2010 and is famous for its red turf field, 'The Inferno'.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: The Evergreen State College
plates.fact: Evergreen State College in Olympia was founded in 1967 with a radically experimental model: no majors, no grades, no traditional departments. Students design their own curriculum in interdisciplinary programs. Notable alumni include Matt Groening (creator of The Simpsons) and Macklemore.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Gonzaga University
plates.fact: Gonzaga's men's basketball team reached its 27th straight NCAA Tournament in 2026. Jesuits founded the school on the Spokane River in 1887, and Bing Crosby studied there before leaving in 1924 to pursue music.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Seattle University
plates.fact: Seattle University is the least-purchased college plate in Washington, with only about 200 registered vehicles — generating just $6,600 annually. The Jesuit university on Capitol Hill was founded in 1891 and is known for its law school and nursing program. Despite its small plate numbers, it has a fiercely loyal alumni base.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Western Washington University
plates.fact: Western Washington University in Bellingham sits between the North Cascades and Puget Sound, with a view of the San Juan Islands on clear days. Founded in 1893, WWU is known for its Huxley College of the Environment — one of the oldest and most respected environmental studies programs in the US.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Law Enforcement Memorial
plates.fact: The Law Enforcement Memorial plate ranks 4th in Washington, with about 11,300 vehicles in 2025. It is open to any driver and supports families of fallen officers.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Professional Firefighter
plates.fact: Fees from the Professional Firefighter plate go to the Washington State Council of Fire Fighters Benevolent Fund, which helps firefighters and their families in times of need.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Volunteer Firefighter
plates.fact: Volunteer firefighters protect much of rural Washington. Fees from this plate go to the Washington State Firefighters' Association.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: 4-H
plates.fact: 4-H reaches nearly 6 million young people across the country, and the four H's stand for Head, Heart, Hands and Health. County fairs east of the Cascades are a big stage for Washington 4-H'ers.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Breast Cancer Awareness
plates.supports: WA Dept. of Health breast, cervical & colon health program
plates.fact: The pink ribbon has stood for breast cancer awareness since the early 1990s. Fees from this plate support the Washington Department of Health's breast, cervical and colon health program.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: FFA Foundation
plates.fact: FFA, founded in 1928 as Future Farmers of America, prepares students for careers in agriculture. Fees from this plate support the FFA Foundation.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2023 report: CY2022 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Fred Hutchinson Cancer Ctr.
plates.fact: Fred Hutch is where Dr. E. Donnall Thomas pioneered bone marrow transplants, work that earned a Nobel Prize in 1990. The center is named for Seattle-raised pitcher Fred Hutchinson, who died of lung cancer in 1964.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Helping Kids Speak
plates.supports: Scottish Rite RiteCare early speech & language clinics
plates.fact: Nearly 1 in 12 U.S. children has a voice, speech or language disorder. This plate supports free early speech and language help from Scottish Rite RiteCare clinics.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: J.P. Patches Pal
plates.fact: The J.P. Patches Show ran on KIRO-TV from 1958 to 1981, starring Edmonds' own Chris Wedes, who died in 2012. It took three tries in the Legislature to get the plate approved, and proceeds support cancer immunotherapy research at Seattle Children's.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Keep Kids Safe
plates.fact: The Keep Kids Safe plate first went on sale on January 3, 2006, and supports work to prevent child abuse and neglect.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Washington Wine Commission
plates.fact: Washington is the nation's second-largest wine producer after California, with more than 1,000 wineries. Most of its grapes grow in the sunny Columbia Valley east of the Cascades.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals (column alignment unclear)

plates.name: We Love Our Pets
plates.supports: WA Federation of Animal Care & Control Agencies
plates.fact: Fees from the We Love Our Pets plate go to the Washington State Federation of Animal Care and Control Agencies, which helps fund spay and neuter programs that mean fewer homeless pets.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Amateur Radio (HAM)
plates.fact: The HAM radio plate uses the operator's actual FCC call sign as the plate number — making every plate unique and instantly recognizable to other operators. Washington has a strong amateur radio tradition, partly due to its rugged terrain making radio essential for emergency communications during earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, and wildfires.

plates.name: Fly Washington Aviation
plates.fact: Boeing was founded in Seattle in 1916, the year its first airplane flew. $28 from each Fly Washington plate funds WSDOT aviation projects, including airport improvements that help with disaster response.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: FY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Music Matters
plates.fact: Seattle's music scene produced Jimi Hendrix, Nirvana, Pearl Jam, Soundgarden, and Macklemore — a disproportionate influence on rock history for one mid-sized city. Music Aid Northwest, supported by this plate, provides instruments and music education to underserved students across Washington.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Share the Road
plates.fact: The Share the Road plate features a cyclist, and its fees support Cascade Bicycle Club. Seattle's Burke-Gilman Trail is one of the busiest multi-use trails in the country.
plates.vehicles_source: DOL 2024 Special License Plate Annual Report: CY2023 original issuances + renewals

plates.name: Square Dancer
plates.supports: No beneficiary — celebration of state dance
plates.fact: Square dancing has been Washington's official state dance since 1979. In 2025 only about 5 vehicles carried this plate, making it the rarest catch on the road.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Throwback Blackout
plates.fact: The Throwback plate has white characters on black, a nod to Washington's 1917–18 plates. It went on sale in November 2025 under the 2025 special-plate law, and its fees support driver training.

plates.name: LeMay Car Museum
plates.supports: LeMay–America's Car Museum (automotive education & job training)
plates.fact: LeMay–America's Car Museum in Tacoma honors Harold LeMay, whose collection of more than 3,000 vehicles was listed by Guinness in 1997 as the world's largest private car collection. The museum opened in 2012, and the plate arrived in 2026.

plates.name: Collector Vehicle
plates.fact: The Collector Vehicle plate is Washington's second most popular specialty plate, with 20,300 registered vehicles generating $710,400 annually. Eligible vehicles must be at least 30 years old and cannot be used for regular transportation like commuting. These are weekend show cars and parade vehicles only.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Horseless Carriage
plates.fact: Since 2026, a Horseless Carriage plate is only for vehicles built before January 1, 1916. Washington began licensing cars in 1905, and S.A. Perkins of Tacoma got the first license for his Pope-Toledo touring car.
plates.vehicles_source: Balk 2025 DOL figures

plates.name: Restored Vehicle
plates.fact: With the Restored plate, owners of classic cars can display a restored original Washington plate from the car's model year, like a 1967 plate on a 1967 Mustang.

plates.name: Rideshare / Vanpool
plates.fact: Rideshare plates are for commuter vehicles that carry a regular group of riders. Qualifying rideshare vans can even be exempt from sales tax.

plates.name: Chehalis Tribe
plates.supports: Tribal members & tribal government only; standard plate pricing (no separate beneficiary)
plates.fact: The Confederated Tribes of the Chehalis Reservation have lived along the Chehalis River since time immemorial, and their reservation near Oakville dates to 1864. Their plate arrived in 2023 and is reserved for tribal members.

plates.name: Muckleshoot Tribe
plates.supports: Tribal members & tribal government only; standard plate pricing (no separate beneficiary)
plates.fact: The Muckleshoot Indian Tribe's reservation lies between the White and Green rivers southeast of Auburn. The tribe's plate, reserved for members, arrived in 2023.

plates.name: Puyallup Tribe
plates.supports: Tribal members & tribal government only; standard plate pricing (no separate beneficiary)
plates.fact: The Puyallup Tribe of Indians, based in Tacoma, signed the Medicine Creek Treaty in 1854 and won a landmark land-claims settlement in the late 1980s. Its plate, reserved for tribal members, arrived in 2025.
